items.title: The Pinnacles (Western Australia)
items.extract: The Pinnacles are limestone formations within Nambung National Park, near the town of Cervantes, Western Australia.

items.title: Tentacled snake
items.extract: The tentacled snake or tentacle snake is a rear-fanged aquatic snake native to Southeast Asia. It is the only species of the genus Erpeton. The two tentacles on its snout are a unique feature among snakes.

items.title: Egg coffee
items.extract: Egg coffee is a Vietnamese drink traditionally prepared with egg yolks, sugar, condensed milk and robusta coffee. The drink is made by filtering coffee beans in a phin, and beating egg yolks with sugar and condensed milk over heat to get egg-cream component.

items.title: Epoch Game Pocket Computer
items.extract: The Epoch Game Pocket Computer, also known as the Game Pokekon , is a second-generation handheld game console released by Epoch Co. in Japan in 1984 for ¥12,800. It is also known as Pokekon.

prompts.text: Name a muscle in the human body

items.title: Stapedius muscle
items.extract: The stapedius is the smallest skeletal muscle in the human body. At just over one millimeter in length, its purpose is to stabilize the smallest bone in the body, the stapes or stirrup bone of the middle ear.

items.title: Zucchetto
items.description: Type of skullcap worn by clergy
items.extract: The zucchetto or solideo, officially a pileolus, is a small, hemispherical, form-fitting ecclesiastical skullcap worn by clerics of the Catholic Church, the Syriac Orthodox Church, and by senior clergy in certain denominations of Lutheranism, Anglicanism, and Methodism.

items.title: The History of Cardenio
items.extract: The History of Cardenio, often referred to as simply Cardenio, is a lost play, known to have been performed by the King's Men, a London theatre company, in 1613. The play is attributed to William Shakespeare and John Fletcher in a Stationers' Register entry of 1653. The content of the play is not known, but it was likely to have been based on an episode in Miguel de Cervantes's Don Quixote involving the character Cardenio, a young man who has been driven mad and lives in the Sierra Morena. Thomas Shelton's translation of the First Part of Don Quixote was published in 1612 and would thus have been available to the presumed authors of the play.
